claim: Early genetic and low-resolution structural observations suggested that extracellular conductive filaments on metal-reducing organisms such as Geobacter were composed of type IV pili.
source: While early genetic and low-resolution structural observations suggested that extracellular conductive filaments on metal-reducing organisms such as Geobacter were composed of type IV pili, it has now been established that bacterial c-type cytochromes can polymerize to form extracellular filaments capable of long-range electron transport.
evidence: This is a historical claim about prior observations in the field, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Bacterial c-type cytochromes can polymerize to form extracellular filaments capable of long-range electron transport.
source: While early genetic and low-resolution structural observations suggested that extracellular conductive filaments on metal-reducing organisms such as Geobacter were composed of type IV pili, it has now been established that bacterial c-type cytochromes can polymerize to form extracellular filaments capable of long-range electron transport.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and is referenced as an established fact.

claim: Atomic structures exist for two cytochrome filaments, formed from the hexaheme cytochrome OmcS and the tetraheme cytochrome OmcE.
source: Atomic structures exist for two such cytochrome filaments, formed from the hexaheme cytochrome OmcS and the tetraheme cytochrome OmcE.
evidence: This claim references existing structural data from prior studies.

claim: OmcS and OmcE have highly conserved heme packing within their central cores.
source: Due to the highly conserved heme packing within the central OmcS and OmcE cores, and shared pattern of heme coordination between subunits, it has been suggested that these polymers have a common origin.
evidence: This claim is based on prior structural observations and is referenced as established knowledge.

claim: OmcS and OmcE share a pattern of heme coordination between subunits.
source: Due to the highly conserved heme packing within the central OmcS and OmcE cores, and shared pattern of heme coordination between subunits, it has been suggested that these polymers have a common origin.
evidence: This claim is based on prior structural observations and is referenced as established knowledge.

claim: It has been suggested that OmcS and OmcE polymers have a common origin.
source: Due to the highly conserved heme packing within the central OmcS and OmcE cores, and shared pattern of heme coordination between subunits, it has been suggested that these polymers have a common origin.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural similarities between OmcS and OmcE.

claim: The structure of a third extracellular filament formed from the Geobacter sulfurreducens octaheme cytochrome OmcZ was determined using cryo-electron microscopy.
source: We have now used cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to determine the structure of a third extracellular filament, formed from the Geobacter sulfurreducens octaheme cytochrome, OmcZ.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the experimental work described in the manuscript.

claim: The packing of hemes in OmcZ is different from OmcS and OmcE.
source: In contrast to the linear heme chains in OmcS and OmcE from the same organism, the packing of hemes, heme:heme angles, and between-subunit heme coordination is quite different in OmcZ.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Heme:heme angles in OmcZ are different from those in OmcS and OmcE.
source: In contrast to the linear heme chains in OmcS and OmcE from the same organism, the packing of hemes, heme:heme angles, and between-subunit heme coordination is quite different in OmcZ.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Between-subunit heme coordination in OmcZ is different from OmcS and OmcE.

claim: OmcZ has a branched heme arrangement.
source: A branched heme arrangement within OmcZ leads to a highly surface exposed heme in every subunit, which may account for the formation of conductive biofilm networks, and explain the higher measured conductivity of OmcZ filaments.
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: OmcZ has a highly surface exposed heme in every subunit.
source: A branched heme arrangement within OmcZ leads to a highly surface exposed heme in every subunit, which may account for the formation of conductive biofilm networks, and explain the higher measured conductivity of OmcZ filaments.

claim: The branched heme arrangement in OmcZ may account for the formation of conductive biofilm networks.

claim: Conductive cytochrome polymers arose independently on more than one occasion from different ancestral multiheme proteins.
source: This new structural evidence suggests that conductive cytochrome polymers arose independently on more than one occasion from different ancestral multiheme proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural differences observed between OmcZ and OmcS/OmcE.

claim: Extracellular electron transfer enables global Fe(III) and Mn(IV) reduction.
source: This process, known as extracellular electron transfer (ET), enables global Fe(III) and Mn(IV) reduction (Gralnick and Newman, 2007; Lovley et al., 2004), methane production in anaerobic digestors (Morita et al., 2011; Shrestha et al., 2013), methane oxidation in ocean seeps (Chadwick et al., 2019), corrosion (Tang et al., 2019), and electricity generation in microbial electrochemical devices (Wang and Ren, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Geobacter organisms establish conductive multicellular biofilms when utilizing conductive surfaces as electron acceptors.
source: When model organisms from the genus Geobacter utilize conductive surfaces as electron acceptors, they establish conductive multicellular biofilms (Chadwick et al., 2019; Yates et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Pili and polysaccharides are essential for the formation of Geobacter biofilms.
source: Many components, including pili and polysaccharides, are essential for the formation of these biofilms (Reguera et al., 2005; Reguera et al., 2007; Rollefson et al., 2011), but the octaheme c-type cytochrome OmcZ is the only cytochrome out of over 80 multiheme proteins in the Geobacter sulfurreducens genome necessary for long-distance conductivity in electrode associated biofilms (Nevin et al., 2009; Peng and Zhang, 2017; Richter et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: OmcZ is the only cytochrome out of over 80 multiheme proteins in the Geobacter sulfurreducens genome necessary for long-distance conductivity in electrode associated biofilms.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Deletion of omcZ affects anodic electron transfer to electrodes.
source: Deletion of omcZ affects anodic ET to electrodes (Nevin et al., 2009; Peng and Zhang, 2017; Richter et al., 2009), especially at low redox potential, and also slows cathodic corrosion of Fe0 (Tang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Deletion of omcZ especially affects anodic electron transfer at low redox potential.

claim: OmcZ is not needed for the reduction of Fe(III) and Mn(IV) oxides.
source: In contrast, OmcZ is not needed for the reduction of other extracellular metals, including Fe(III) and Mn(IV) oxides (Aklujkar et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The omcZ gene (GSU2076) is upregulated 400–800% in conductive electrode biofilms.
source: The omcZ gene (GSU2076) is upregulated 400–800% in conductive electrode biofilms (Franks et al., 2012; Nevin et al., 2009), producing a 50 kDa periplasmic preprotein that is processed by the OzpA protease (GSU2075) to a 30 kDa octaheme form (Inoue et al., 2010; Jiménez Otero et al., 2018; Kai et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Similar operons containing homologous omcZ and ozpA are widespread throughout the Bacterial and Archaeal domains.

claim: OmcZ molecules have a wide heme reduction potential window (-420 mV to –60 mV vs. SHE).
source: In G. sulfurreducens, large heat-stable OmcZ molecules with a wide heme reduction potential window (-420 mV to –60 mV vs. the standard hydrogen electrode [SHE]) are abundant in the extracellular matrix between cells (Inoue et al., 2011), which under atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging appear as ~2.5 nm diameter conductive filaments (Yalcin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of G. sulfurreducens OmcS and OmcE reveal a core of closely spaced c-type hemes.
source: Cryo-EM structures of G. sulfurreducens OmcS and OmcE, which are involved in ET to insoluble Fe(III) and Mn(IV), reveal a core of closely spaced c-type hemes, with the unique characteristic of histidine residues from the previous subunit coordinating a heme from the next.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior structural studies.

claim: Higher pH buffers were found to increase the recovery of OmcZ.
source: Filaments were enriched via shearing, DNAse treatment and salt precipitation, similar to protocols used for OmcS and OmcE, except that higher pH buffers were found to increase the recovery of OmcZ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: OmcZ filaments did not show as strong a sinusoidal morphology as OmcS filaments.

evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.
